name: startup_build_command_and_run
description: Program entry point. It finds the current process and, depending on whether its command-line pointer is set, either runs a directory and file open sequence or copies the process name and argument text into a stack buffer. It then calls the shared setup and cleanup routines and returns.

name: release_saved_handles_and_return
description: Calls a shared cleanup routine, releases two saved handles through library function pointers when they are non-zero, and returns the parameter together with a saved value.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library functions through fixed negative offsets from the library base register, one after the other, and returns.

name: open_dos_library_or_fail
description: Opens the dos library by name through a library function at a fixed offset and returns the handle when it is non-zero. On failure it calls a cleanup routine and returns the constant 100.

name: split_arguments_and_open_console
description: Splits the NUL-terminated argument string into at most 32 whitespace-separated words and stores a pointer to each in a global table. It then sets mode values from a flag, opens the standard input and output handles, and calls the shared setup and cleanup routines.

name: allocate_and_init_block
description: Allocates a memory block of the requested size plus twelve bytes, stores that size in the block header, calls an initialization routine with a global and the block address, and returns the block address plus twelve, or zero if the allocation fails.

name: allocate_block_or_fail
description: Calls the block allocator with the given size and returns its result, or minus one when that result is zero.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns the all-bits-set value, which is minus one, without any other work.

name: free_linked_memory_blocks
description: Walks a linked list whose head is held in a global variable. For each node it releases the node memory using the size stored in the node, then follows the next pointer until the list is empty.

name: append_node_to_list
description: Inserts the second node at the tail of a list whose head and tail pointers sit in the first structure. It clears the new node's next link, links the old tail to it, updates the tail, and sets the head when the list was empty.

name: load_zmachine_story_header
description: Checks that the story version byte is four and otherwise reports a wrong-version error. It then reads the dictionary, object table and globals table offsets from the header and computes the addresses of those tables in memory.

name: check_objtab_alignment_flag
description: Reads a 16-bit flags word from a structure at a fixed offset. When its lowest bit is set it calls several routines and returns the result of the last call, otherwise it returns the flags word; its referenced text reports an object table alignment error.

name: shift_result_right_nine
description: Calls a routine and returns its result shifted right by nine bits, which divides the value by 512.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; two routines call it as an empty hook.

name: store_word_big_endian
description: Writes the low 16 bits of the data register to the address held in the address register, high byte first.

name: compare_limit_and_advance
description: Compares its word argument with a limit from the global block and calls one of two routines depending on the result. When the value that routine returns is 511, it adds one to the argument and returns the argument with that value.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two routines one after the other and returns, with no other work.

name: read_byte_and_advance
description: Reads one byte from a buffer whose base pointer is held in a global slot, at the index stored in the global block, then advances that index by one. When the index passes 511 it calls a routine that reports the overflow.

name: read_word_big_endian
description: Calls the byte reader twice and returns the first byte shifted left by eight bits, combined with the second byte as the low part.

name: read_operand_by_type
description: Reads an operand selected by a type argument. Zero or negative types read a two-byte big-endian value, type one reads a byte from the buffer and advances the index, and other types fetch a value from a table chosen by a second routine's result.

name: read_variable_by_number
description: Returns a 16-bit variable chosen by a number. Zero returns the word at the address held in the pointer register, numbers below sixteen index a local table, and larger numbers index a global table.

name: store_variable_by_number
description: Stores a 16-bit value into a variable chosen by a number. Zero writes the word at the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: shift_value_right_nine
description: Returns its 16-bit input shifted right by nine bits.

name: extract_high_byte
description: Returns the upper eight bits of its 16-bit input by shifting it right by eight bits.

name: shift_value_right_seven
description: Returns its 16-bit input shifted right by seven bits.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls a routine for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls a routine for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls a routine for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: decode_branch_and_jump
description: Decodes a branch from one or two offset bytes, including its condition bit. Offsets zero and one return false and true, and any other offset moves the program position by that offset, adjusting the page and cached address.

name: decode_branch_and_jump
description: Decodes a branch from one or two offset bytes, including its condition bit. Offsets zero and one return false and true, and any other offset moves the program position by that offset, adjusting the page and cached address.

name: scale_input_by_constant
description: Masks the input to its low sixteen bits and multiplies the result by fourteen, returning the product.

name: read_table_byte_doubled
description: Calls a routine for an index, reads the byte at that index from a table whose base is held in a global slot, and returns the byte multiplied by two.

name: read_variable_length_byte
description: Reads a byte from the address register. If its top bit is clear it returns that byte, otherwise it returns the low six bits of the following byte.

name: fetch_operands_then_store
description: Calls three routines to fetch its operands, then stores the result into the destination chosen by the returned number. Zero writes the word before the pointer register, and other numbers write a local or global table slot.

name: store_word_at_indexed_address
description: Computes an address from a base pointer in a global slot plus two register offsets scaled by two, then writes the word there in big-endian order.

name: store_byte_at_indexed_address
description: Writes one byte at the global base address plus the sum of its two register offsets.

name: scan_then_store_word
description: Repeats a routine while a counter is below the low six bits of the byte at the address register, then stores the returned word. The destination is the word before the pointer for zero, otherwise a local or global table slot.

name: scan_then_store_word
description: Repeats a routine until a counter reaches the low six bits of the byte at the address register, then stores the returned word. The destination is the word before the pointer for zero, otherwise a local or global table slot.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls a routine for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: store_variable_by_number
description: Stores a 16-bit value into a variable chosen by a number. Zero writes the word at the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: increment_and_store_variable
description: Calls a routine to read a value, adds one to it, and stores the result into a destination selected by a number. Zero writes the word at the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: compare_value_and_branch
description: Compares a value from a routine with a second argument and calls one of two routines based on the result. It then decodes a branch from one or two offset bytes, returning false or true for offsets zero and one and otherwise moving the program position by the offset.

name: tokenise_text_into_entries
description: Splits the input text into words at separator characters taken from a table, and for each word writes a four-byte entry holding its start position and length. Scanning stops at the end of the buffer or the word limit.

name: continue_text_tokenising
description: Resumes the word split from the middle of the tokeniser loop, writing word entries and handling separator characters in the same way as the main scan.

name: handle_tokeniser_separator
description: Handles a character that matches a separator during tokenising. When no word is open it records the separator as a word of its own, otherwise it closes the current word entry and continues the scan.

name: report_too_many_words
description: Continues the word split and, as its referenced text shows, reports that too many words were typed and discards the rest of the input.

name: finish_word_entry_loop
description: Writes the entry for the current word, then repeats the separator scan until the word limit or end of text is reached.

name: store_parsed_word_count
description: Writes the current word count into the second byte of the parse header that a global slot points to.

name: read_input_line_lowercase
description: Reads characters from the input routine into a buffer until a carriage return, removing the previous character on backspace and lowercasing uppercase letters, then returns the line length.

name: continue_input_line_read
description: Continues line input from a first character already held in the data register. It stores characters, handles backspace and carriage return, lowercases the line when it ends, and returns its length.

name: read_input_chars_until_return
description: Reads input characters into the line buffer until carriage return or backspace, moving the write position on backspace and stopping when the buffer is full.

name: lowercase_and_measure_input
description: Converts uppercase letters in the input buffer to lowercase up to the end position, when the conversion flag is set, and returns the number of characters read.

name: compute_pointer_difference
description: Returns the difference between the address register and a second address register.

name: binary_search_dictionary
description: Performs a binary search over a sorted dictionary table, comparing the search word with entries and halving the range each step until the matching entry is found or the range is exhausted, then returns the entry address.

name: binary_search_dictionary
description: Continues a binary search over a sorted dictionary table, comparing the search word with entries and narrowing the range by halves, and returns the entry address on a match.

name: binary_search_dictionary
description: Continues a binary search over a sorted dictionary table from the current bounds, moving the lower bound forward on each comparison and returning the entry address when the word matches.

name: write_output_character
description: Converts a tab character to a space, writes the character to the output buffer, and advances the buffer pointer. It also handles word spacing state before writing when the state flags are set.

name: write_decimal_number
description: Converts a signed 16-bit value to decimal digits by repeated division by ten, passes the digits to an output routine in order, and writes a zero character to the buffer.

name: encode_dictionary_word
description: Encodes the characters of a word as five-bit codes packed three to a 16-bit word, using the alphabet shifts for characters outside the first set, and sets the end bit on the final word.

name: select_block_for_address
description: Splits a 16-bit address into a block number and an offset inside a 512-byte block. When the block differs from the cached one, it loads the new block through a routine and records its base address.

name: return_value_to_variable
description: Restores the saved frame pointer and program position from the call frame, then stores the returned word into the variable selected by the frame's store number. It returns the high byte of the value.

name: write_newline_to_output
description: Writes a carriage return to the output buffer when the output-state word is set, then calls two output routines when their flags are set.

name: store_global_word
description: Stores the 16-bit argument into a fixed global cell.

name: set_output_stream_state
description: Selects or deselects an output stream from its argument: zero clears the stream flag, while one sets it and saves the current position and table address returned by a routine.

name: clear_saved_long_value
description: Calls a routine that returns zero and stores that 32-bit value into the saved state at a fixed frame offset, clearing it.

name: set_flag_by_argument
description: When the argument is one it sets the flag word to one and clears the argument. When the argument is zero it calls a routine with the argument and clears the flag word.

name: apply_stream_control_code
description: Decodes a stream control code. Minus one and one clear and set the first flag, minus two and two clear and set the second flag while updating a bit in the status byte, and other codes are adjusted and passed to a routine or used to record a buffer pointer.

name: apply_stream_control_code
description: Handles negative stream control codes: minus one clears the first flag and minus two clears the second flag and a bit in the status byte. Any other argument is shifted by three and, when the result is zero and a flag is set, a routine is called.

name: enable_output_flag
description: Sets the output flag word at a fixed frame offset to one.

name: clear_output_flag
description: Clears the output flag word at a fixed frame offset to zero.

name: set_second_flag_and_bit
description: Sets the second flag word to one and sets the lowest bit of the status byte in the story memory header, then calls a routine.

name: clear_second_flag_and_bit
description: Clears the second flag word and the lowest bit of the status byte in the story memory header, then calls a routine.

name: start_buffered_output
description: Computes an output pointer from a base address plus a word offset in the argument, stores it, and sets the buffered-output flag.

name: end_buffered_output
description: When the buffered-output flag is set, clears the flag and calls a routine to flush the buffer.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls routines for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: increment_or_forward_value
description: For a non-zero argument it returns the argument plus one. For zero it calls a routine and then passes two saved globals to a further routine.

name: decrement_and_call_if_zero
description: Subtracts one from the argument and calls a routine when the result is zero.

name: store_zero_based_position
description: Adds a saved base offset to the first argument when the stream flag is clear, stores the first and second arguments minus one into two saved fields, and calls a routine.

name: finish_output_sequence
description: Calls a sequence of output routines, calling extra ones when a stored pointer is non-zero or a flag is zero, and returns the result of the last call.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two routines one after the other and returns, with no other work.

name: call_routine_with_arguments
description: Saves the caller's frame and program position, pushes the given number of argument words, calls a routine, and stores its returned word into the destination selected by the call's store number.

name: advance_program_position
description: Adds the argument minus two to the packed position, splits the result into a block number and an offset, and loads a new block through a routine when the block changes.

name: return_value_to_variable
description: Restores the saved frame state from the call frame and stores the returned word into the variable selected by the frame's store number, handling the zero case as the other store routines do. It returns the high byte of the value.

name: call_routine_and_store
description: Builds a call frame on the stack, saves the program position and frame pointer, calls a routine, and stores its result into the destination selected by the store number.

name: store_word_by_variable_number
description: Calls routines for a number and stores the value into the destination it selects. Zero writes the word two bytes before the pointer register, numbers below sixteen write a local table slot, and larger numbers write a global table slot.

name: dispatch_next_instruction
description: Reads the next opcode byte and dispatches on its top bits: short, long and variable forms each decode their operands, and the low four bits select the matching operation through a switch.

name: report_bad_operation
description: Runs a sequence of routines and, depending on a flag, further routines; its referenced text reads Bad operation.

name: encode_dictionary_word
description: Encodes the characters of a word as five-bit codes packed three to a 16-bit word, using the alphabet shifts for characters outside the first set, and sets the end bit on the final word.

name: classify_character_class
description: Classifies a character into one of a few classes: zero, uppercase letters, other non-lowercase characters, and lowercase letters, which take a different path.

name: classify_character_class
description: Classifies a character into one of a few classes: zero, uppercase letters, other non-lowercase characters, and lowercase letters, which take a different path.

name: classify_uppercase_letter
description: Returns one for an uppercase letter and two for any other character.

name: find_alphabet_index
description: Scans a null-terminated alphabet table for the character in the data register and, on a match, reduces an offset into the five-bit range by repeated subtraction of twenty-six.

name: reduce_to_five_bits
description: Subtracts twenty-six from a value repeatedly while it is above thirty-one, reducing it into the five-bit range.

name: encode_text_to_zchars
description: Converts up to nine characters into five-bit codes, using the alphabet shifts for characters outside the first set, and stores them in a buffer of three-code groups for packing.

name: pack_zchars_into_words
description: Pads the Z-character buffer with the padding code five, then packs groups of three five-bit codes into three bytes, setting the end bit on the last byte.

name: initialize_buffer_structure
description: Initializes a seven-word structure in place: it points the first link at the structure body, stores the two arguments in two fields, clears a counter and a flag byte, and calls a routine first.

name: write_output_character
description: Converts a tab character to a space, writes the character to the output buffer, and advances the buffer pointer. It also handles word spacing state before writing when the state flags are set.

name: write_wrapped_output_character
description: Writes a character into a line buffer and wraps the text at a word boundary when the line width is reached, flushing the buffer at carriage return.

name: reset_output_line_buffer
description: Clears the column counter of the output structure, calls a routine, records the buffer start, and sets the flag byte.

name: start_output_line_buffer
description: Calls a routine, copies the buffer start into the write position and sets the flag byte to one.

name: echo_input_character
description: Reads a character through a routine and echoes it through an output routine when the echo flag is clear, except that backspace is not echoed while the position is zero.

name: write_wrapped_input_character
description: Adds a typed character to the input line buffer, wrapping at word boundaries when the line width is reached and handling carriage return as the end of the line.

name: loop_until_address_match
description: When its flag is set, repeatedly calls a routine until the address register matches the data register, then calls another routine.

name: select_block_for_address
description: Splits a 16-bit address into a block number and an offset inside a 512-byte block. When the block differs from the cached one, it loads the new block through a routine and records its base address.

name: find_cached_block
description: Looks up a block number in a table of cached blocks. When the number differs from the last one it updates the use counter, finds the matching entry, reads the block through a routine when needed, and marks the entry most recently used.

name: find_least_recent_cache_slot
description: Scans the cache table for the entry with the smallest use counter and returns its address, computed from the table base and a 64-byte entry size.

name: report_story_open_error
description: Calls a sequence of routines to report a failure when the previous check did not succeed; its referenced text reads Story file open error.

name: report_memory_allocation_error
description: When an allocation result is zero, calls a sequence of routines to report the failure; its referenced text reads Memory block allocation error.

name: report_insufficient_memory
description: Calls one routine to report the condition; its referenced text says there is not enough available memory.

name: forward_word_argument
description: Passes its word argument to a routine and returns.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other work.

name: return_saved_word_pair
description: Calls a routine, then returns two saved global words combined into one result.

name: save_word_pair_and_call
description: Saves its two word arguments into global cells, then calls a routine. The routine's referenced text includes a story file close error and a strike-any-key message.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; the code is an empty routine in the unreached gap.

name: echo_input_character
description: Reads a character through a routine and echoes it through an output routine when the echo flag is clear, except that backspace is not echoed while the position is zero.

name: read_key_press
description: Reads keys until a character at or above space arrives, ending on carriage return or backspace, and maps the delete key to backspace.

name: clear_input_mode_flag
description: Clears the flag word at a fixed frame offset to zero, then calls a routine.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other work.

name: flush_when_line_full
description: Compares the remaining line space, computed from two saved values, with a counter. When they match it calls a routine and resets the counter to one.

name: clear_input_mode_flag
description: Clears the flag word at a fixed frame offset to zero, then calls a routine.

name: flush_pending_output_range
description: When the stream flag is clear it calls a routine. It then compares the two addresses, and when they differ and the start is not after the end, calls another routine with the difference.

name: increment_output_counter
description: Calls two routines, then adds one to the counter at a fixed frame offset when the stream flag is clear.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; the code is an empty routine.

name: print_zero_terminated_text
description: Passes each byte of a zero-terminated string to an output routine until the terminator, then calls another routine when the flag word is set and returns its result.

name: report_internal_error
description: Finishes an output line: when the argument is non-zero it calls a routine, and it writes a carriage return and calls output routines depending on the flags. Its referenced text reads Internal Error.

name: branch_on_header_flag
description: Tests the lowest bit of the status byte in the story memory header and calls one of two routines depending on the result, returning zero when the bit is set.

name: call_and_clear_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and, when the condition flag is set, calls a second routine and returns zero.

name: forward_word_argument
description: Passes its word argument to a routine and returns.

name: stop_scripting_on_printer_error
description: Clears the scripting bit in the story memory header and the printer flag, then calls two routines. Its referenced text reads that the printer is not ready and scripting is terminated.

name: call_routine_if_nonzero
description: Calls a routine and, when its result is non-zero, calls a second routine.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; it is an empty routine.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; it is an empty routine.

name: store_pending_value_on_success
description: Calls a routine, and when it returns zero stores a saved global into the pending-value slot at a fixed frame offset and returns zero.

name: consume_pending_value
description: Passes the pending value at a fixed frame offset to a routine, then clears that slot to zero.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other work.

name: report_story_read_error
description: Calls a routine with the saved pending value and its arguments, then reports through a sequence of routines when the result is non-zero. Its referenced text reads Story file read error.

name: read_uppercase_letter
description: Reads characters through a routine, folding lowercase letters to uppercase and skipping any that are not letters, until a carriage return or a letter arrives.

name: check_first_answer_letter
description: Reads a character and scans the buffer, skipping spaces, for the first character that is not a space. Returns zero when that character is y, otherwise one.

name: call_and_recover_on_zero
description: Calls a routine with the arguments one and zero, and calls a second routine when that result is zero.

name: store_pending_value_on_success
description: Calls a routine; when it returns zero it stores a saved global into the pending-value slot and returns zero, otherwise it calls a second routine.

name: return_argument_after_call
description: Calls a routine and returns the argument register value.

name: handle_result_code
description: Calls a routine with the pending value. When the result is non-zero it calls one of two routines depending on whether the result equals 999.

name: report_disk_full
description: Calls a routine to report the condition; its referenced text reads Not enough room on disk.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; it is an empty routine.

name: forward_pending_value
description: Passes the pending value at a fixed frame offset to a routine and returns.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other work.

name: forward_high_word
description: Passes the upper sixteen bits of the data register to a routine, with the low bits cleared.

name: call_routine_with_one
description: Calls a routine with the constant one.

name: report_icon_file_error
description: Calls a routine and, when its result is non-zero, calls a second routine; its referenced text reads Couldn't create icon file.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; it is an empty routine.

name: prompt_for_save_file
description: Runs a series of routines for the save-file prompt. When the selected index is zero it calls a routine with zero, otherwise it clears the global entry at that index. Its referenced text asks for the save disk and a file name.

name: call_routine_with_zero
description: Calls a routine with the constant zero, then calls a second routine.

name: invoke_system_trap
description: Stores its argument in a global cell and executes the trap instruction with number one.

name: perform_device_io_command
description: Fills the device request's data, offset and command fields from its two arguments and the command code three, then runs the synchronous device I/O routine on it.

name: send_device_io_command
description: Sets the request command code to two and two further request fields, then sends the request asynchronously through the device send routine.

name: wait_for_message_reply
description: Waits on the port, takes the next message from it, calls a routine, and returns the first byte of the message.

name: send_control_sequence
description: Writes the byte 155 followed by a zero byte into a two-byte buffer, the control sequence introducer, then writes the argument and a routine result to output.

name: read_string_until_terminator
description: Skips input bytes until the marker byte of minus 101 arrives, then copies the following bytes into a buffer, resetting the length on each marker, until the given terminator byte, and ends the string with zero.

name: read_bytes_until_marker
description: Reads bytes through a routine into a buffer, ending it with zero, until the marker byte of minus 101 arrives; a matching terminator byte resets the buffer length.

name: store_byte_and_terminate
description: Writes the byte at a fixed frame offset into the buffer at the index held in a frame slot, then writes a zero terminator after it.

name: beep_on_code_two
description: When the argument is two it calls the display beep routine on a window pointer taken from a global structure; other values do nothing.

name: read_current_time
description: Calls the system clock routine, which writes the seconds and microseconds into two local cells.

name: dispatch_by_mode_code
description: Selects one of several calls according to a small mode number from zero to four, passing the global block to the same routine in each case and falling through the cases.

name: pass_global_block_to_routine
description: Passes the address of the global block to a routine.

name: pass_global_block_to_routine
description: Passes the address of the global block to a routine.

name: pass_global_block_to_routine
description: Passes the address of the global block to a routine.

name: pass_global_block_to_routine
description: Passes the address of the global block to a routine.

name: compute_grid_dimensions
description: Computes the width and height of a grid from the window bounds minus margins, divides them by two cell sizes, stores the quotients and remainders in globals, and clamps the saved column and row limits.

name: reset_grid_cursor
description: Sets the saved column limit to the cell count minus one and clears the saved row position.

name: write_cursor_position_sequence
description: Converts the current row and column, each plus one, into text in two 32-byte buffers and writes them into a cursor-position escape sequence, then sends that sequence to output.

name: advance_output_line
description: Moves to the next output line: when the column is before the last column it writes a carriage return and line feed, otherwise it returns the column to the saved start, clears the row, and calls routines that handle the wrap.

name: pass_global_block_to_routine
description: Passes the address of the global block to a routine.

name: clear_column_range
description: Loops over columns from the first argument up to the second, setting the column and clearing the row, and calls two routines for each column. It then restores the saved position.

name: clear_grid_region
description: Resets the saved column and row to zero, calls two routines, moves the column to the last cell, and calls another routine.

name: forward_with_extended_count
description: Passes its pointer argument and its 16-bit count, widened to 32 bits, to a routine.

name: write_terminal_character
description: Writes a carriage return through a routine, writes backspace as the three-byte sequence backspace, space, backspace, and writes any other character as a single byte.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns without other work.

name: display_more_prompt
description: Writes a pad string and the [MORE] prompt through output routines, waits for input, and erases the prompt.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it does nothing; it is an empty routine.

name: output_global_block
description: Passes the global block to an output routine on both branches, so the argument makes no difference to what is written.

name: output_global_block
description: Passes the global block to an output routine twice.

name: trim_string_spaces
description: Skips leading space characters, then removes trailing spaces by replacing them with zero terminators.

name: trim_trailing_spaces
description: Removes trailing space characters from the string at the argument by replacing them with zero terminators.

name: find_path_separator_end
description: Searches the string for a slash and, when none is found, for a colon, and returns the position just after the match, or zero when neither exists.

name: split_directory_and_file_name
description: Looks for a path separator in the global text. Without one it copies the text into a buffer; with one it splits the text at the last separator, writing zero terminators and copying the parts into the global block.

name: forward_saved_pointer
description: Passes the pointer saved in the frame to a routine.

name: read_file_block_at_offset
description: Seeks to the requested offset when the position differs from the last one, reads the requested byte count into the buffer, and records the new position and the status or I/O error code.

name: write_file_block_at_offset
description: Seeks to the requested offset, writes the given byte count from the buffer, and records the I/O error code when the seek or write fails.

name: write_buffer_to_file
description: Writes the buffer to the open file through the write routine, stores the byte count it returns, and records the I/O error code when the count is minus one or differs from the requested count.

name: stub_compare_without_effect
description: Compares two frame values and does nothing with the result, returning zero.

name: open_new_file
description: Opens the named file in new-file mode and records the handle, reading the I/O error code when the open fails.

name: open_existing_file
description: Opens the named file in old-file mode and records the handle, reading the I/O error code when the open fails.

name: close_file_handle
description: Closes the file handle passed as the argument.

name: delete_named_file
description: Deletes the file named in the global text; the result is not acted on.

name: test_file_write_lock
description: Tries to lock the named file for writing. When the lock fails it sets the flag, otherwise it clears the flag and releases the lock.

name: set_flag_and_return_saved
description: Sets the flag to one and returns the value saved in the frame.

name: open_story_data_file
description: Opens the story data file by name in old-file mode, recording the handle and reading the I/O error code on failure.

name: close_file_handle
description: Closes the file handle passed as the argument.

name: write_icon_file
description: Sets two icon position fields to a sentinel value and writes the disk object through the icon library. It returns zero on success or the I/O error code, and one when no object is held.

name: write_icon_file
description: Sets two icon position fields to a sentinel value and writes the disk object through the icon library, returning the I/O error code or zero on success.
